Before being allowed to race again, AUTUMN VIBES will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

B Avdulla pleaded guilty to a careless riding charge for causing interference leaving the 900 Metres (see CALL TO COMMAND).  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Trainer W K Mo confirmed that he had instructed B Avdulla to go forward on the horse as it had not been finishing its races off most recently and he was of the opinion that with sheepskin cheek pieces being applied today and the horse being one-paced it would be advantageous to hold a more forward position.

Badly crowded shortly after the start.  Apprentice P N Wong stated that her instructions were to lead but after receiving interference shortly after the start she was unable to do so.  She said RUBY SAILING raced very wide and without cover for the majority of the event before giving ground in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be a "roarer” which had previously been reported and also found it to have sustained an abrasion to its right hind leg.
Making the turn leaving the 900 Metres became unbalanced and ran wider.

Shortly after the start was bumped by BASIC INSTINCT which shifted out before being corrected by its rider.  B Avdulla (HAPPY BOYS) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that leaving the 900 Metres he allowed his mount to shift in when not clear of CALL TO COMMAND, resulting in CALL TO COMMAND having to be checked when crowded and also when shifting out blundered when it struck the heels of HAPPY BOYS and further resulting in BASIC INSTINCT having to be checked when crowded between CALL TO COMMAND and SMART TRIO.  Having regard to Jockey Avdulla holding confirmed riding engagements for the remainder of the season and in accordance with previous practices, he was fined the sum of $35,000 in lieu of a one-day suspension.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his very good race riding record.  L Hewitson stated that after being crowded shortly after the start and then checked leaving the 900 Metres his mount was unable to finish the race off in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be a "roarer” which had previously been reported and also found it to have sustained an abrasion to its left front leg.

When questioned regarding his riding in the Home Straight and the reason he elected to shift to the outside of MASTER LUCKY near the 250 Metres, J Orman stated that his instructions were to hold a midfield position but he was issued with no specific instructions as to where to position the horse in the Home Straight.  He said after following HAROLD WIN into the race he observed a run become available between HAROLD WIN and MASTER LUCKY at which point he then started to ride his mount along to improve.  He said under its top weight of 135 lbs JOYFUL JOY did not respond strongly to his efforts and as he was concerned that the run between MASTER LUCKY and HAROLD WIN might close, he elected to shift JOYFUL JOY to the outside of MASTER LUCKY near the 250 Metres to secure clear running.  He added that after making contact with SOLID CAR, his mount became unbalanced before continuing to respond to his riding but did not make any appreciable ground on the first or second placegetters.  Trainer M Newnham confirmed the instructions and stated that, in his opinion, Jockey Orman would have been better suited by persevering for the run between HAROLD WIN and MASTER LUCKY.  After considering his explanations and the manner in which JOYFUL JOY finished the race off, the Stewards advised Jockey Orman that, in their opinion, he had made an error of judgement by shifting to the outside of MASTER LUCKY when the run remained available between MASTER LUCKY and HAROLD WIN.  Sent for sampling post-race.
